references.text: Moses predicted this night when all the firstborn in Egypt would die, and that there would be a great cry throughout all of Egypt, greater than ever before.
The Lord had announced that He would strike down all the firstborn in Egypt that night, and that the blood on the doorposts would serve as a sign to protect the Israelites.
The verse just before describes the actual event where the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn to the captive's firstborn and every firstborn of the livestock.
The Egyptians buried all their firstborn whom the Lord had struck among them when the Israelites departed.
The psalm recalls how God struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in Ham's tents.
The psalm describes how the Lord struck down all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their strength.
The psalm praises the Lord who struck down Egypt's firstborn, both humans and livestock.
The psalm extols the Lord who struck the Egyptians through their firstborn, for His mercy endures forever.
Amos refers to the plague in Egypt and the stench from the camps, which recalls the death that befell Egypt.
Hebrews mentions that Moses by faith kept the Passover and applied the blood, so that the destroyer would not touch the Israelites' firstborn.
Prophetic precursor: Exodus 11:6 warns of the great cry that is then realized in Exodus 12:30.
Thematic parallel: Both emphasize that judgment strikes every single house without exception, underscoring God's total intervention.
Theological contrast: The groaning of Israel's children out of fear or doubt (Num 14) stands in sharp contrast to the Egyptians' cry under judgment (Ex 12).
Same event with a dual perspective: 12:30 describes the judgment on Egypt, while 12:42 interprets the night as God's act of salvation for Israel.
Theological contrast: The groaning of Israel's children for deliverance (Ex 2) stands in contrast to the Egyptians' cry under judgment (Ex 12).
Prophetic fulfillment: The servants' prayer in 11:8 to let the people go is realized when Pharaoh himself drives them out in 12:30.
